authoring: Use the relevant file section and its schema at this guide revision. Draft from the story, agreed criteria, and verified documentation, skills, and tools. Flag unknowns for human review.

Review the checklist, criteria, and roster together. A human supplies subject-matter expertise, then the Implementation Lead checks references, permissions, assignments, and tester independence before dispatch.
Use public names or aliases in viewer files. Keep credentials, private runtime identifiers, fixtures, and restricted evidence in approved private storage.

title.label: Story ID and title
title.help: Use a stable story ID and a title that names the outcome.

owner.label: Owner
owner.help: Name the person accountable for the story outcome and acceptance decision. Use Pending confirmation if unknown.

outcome.label: Outcome
outcome.help: Name the actor, the capability they need, and the benefit.

scope.label: Scope
scope.help: State what the story delivers and verifies. Name relevant exclusions.

operations.label: Operations
operations.help: Describe the trigger, repeatable action, and observable result when it clarifies the story.

acceptance.label: Acceptance
acceptance.help: Record the authorized human decision for this story, its scope and remaining criteria. Use Pending decision until confirmed.

requirements.label: Requirements and verification
requirements.help: Link to scenarios.json for criteria and verification definitions.

files.label: Files
files.help: Link to the checklist and the other story files in use. Add a short purpose for each link.

adminGuidance.label: Admin guidance
adminGuidance.help: Record verified maintenance or replay steps and link to the runbook when applicable.

next.label: Next
next.help: State the next activity. Link to a blocker if it affects that activity.
next.authoring: For an active story, record the next milestone and any parallel work ready to start. At closure, record completion or final handoff.

checklist.json.$comment: Field guidance for the task checklist, rendered by the viewer and read by agents one field at a time. Resolve relative reference URLs from this file. Data rules live in checklist.schema.json.

task.label: Task
task.help: Name one build or setup action a single executor can finish. The story describes the repeatable operation it supports.
task.example: Run baseline extraction on the pilot PDF.
task.handoff: Send only this task, the outputs and evidence of its Requires tasks, its inputs, expected output, Task AC and guardrails. Cite supported checks or scenarios by ID.

status.label: Status
status.ai: Suggest a fixed status from the evidence. Explain exceptions in Comments.
status.review: Use Pass only when the Task AC is met and evidence is recorded.

comments.label: Comments
comments.help: Record what happened and the next action. For a failed or blocked check, name the reason, follow-up and its owner. Keep earlier comments and evidence inline or by link.
comments.example: Retest returned unrelated policy text. Recheck in S-07; refine in S-08 if the error persists.

ownerType.label: Owner type
ownerType.ai: Use Automation for test runs, AI for drafting or review, and Human for acceptance. Split tasks when the executor changes.
ownerType.review: Confirm who runs the check, who reviews the evidence, and who can accept the result.

uiQa.label: UI QA?
uiQa.help: Yes when a browser journey, layout, or interaction needs checking. Record the actual result in Result evidence.
checklist: Open the affected screen as the intended user.
Check the main path and a meaningful failure case.
Record the browser, build, and result.

mobileQa.label: Mobile QA?
mobileQa.help: Yes when a mobile layout, native interaction, or device capability needs checking. Record the actual result in Result evidence.
checklist: Use the intended device or emulator, app build, and user role.
Check the main path and a mobile-specific interaction.
Use a real device if required hardware behavior is unproven.
Record the device or emulator, OS, build, and observed result.

value.label: Value
value.help: Say who benefits and what improves, such as accuracy, speed, or decision quality.
value.example: Reviewers avoid treating unrelated policy as the bid’s payment terms.

reusableArtifact.label: Reusable artifact
reusableArtifact.help: Describe the reusable template or script and record whether preparing it is planned.

example.description: Extraction workbook with a synthetic sample.

githubFile.label: Published GitHub file
githubFile.help: Link the exact published file. Show the full URL when the artifact is planned and the task reaches Pass.

requires.label: Requires
requires.help: List direct prerequisite task IDs. Each must reach Pass before starting. Omit when there are none.
requires.ai: Skip IDs already required by another listed task. Read the required outputs and evidence.

inputs.label: Expected inputs
inputs.help: List the artifacts, fixture or starting state, and access needed for the task and check. Identify the input revision when it affects the result. Put prerequisite tasks in Requires.
inputs.example: Pilot PDF, baseline JSON, and test processor version.

outputs.label: Expected outputs
outputs.help: Name the deliverable and format. If it uses a published template, link the exact GitHub template file here.
outputs.example: Raw extraction JSON and a Markdown comparison table. Link the published table template if one exists.

metric.label: Success metric
metric.help: Optional. Name what to maximize or minimize, how to measure it, and the guardrail. Mark untested targets Proposed.
metric.example: Minimize time to find the bucket owner. Proposed: two minutes, with correct ownership.

completion.label: Task AC
completion.help: Name the check type and observable pass rule. Give the bounded steps or link the exact versioned test, runbook or criterion that defines them. Use Supports when the cited criterion defines the procedure. Include a meaningful failure case when relevant.
completion.example: UI smoke check. Run A-01 on all three fixtures. Pass if only the overdue unpaid invoice shows the flag.

supports.label: Supports checks or scenarios
supports.help: IDs of story criteria, checks or scenarios this task supports. Omit when none.
supports.ai: Read only the cited criteria, checks or scenarios needed for this task.
supports.review: Use the story for inline check results and private run records for structured scenarios.

evidence.label: Result evidence
evidence.help: Files or records that show what actually happened. Put blockers and next steps in Comments.
evidence.ai: Link the actual run or review. Record revision, tool and observed result. For AI review, record model and reasoning if known.
evidence.review: Check the artifact proves the named test or review ran on the stated revision and surface.
evidence.example: Link the Playwright run or trace for the tested revision. Link code review findings separately.

scope.label: Scope
scope.help: Name the documents, fields, or decisions this task covers. Say what is out of scope.
scope.example: Retest payment terms on the same PDF. Exclude general policy pages.

direction.label: Solution approach
direction.help: Name the runner, build, environment, and fixture. Link the repeatable command or manual test steps.
direction.example: Playwright on Chromium against the local preview with a synthetic checklist.

guardrails.label: Guardrails
guardrails.help: Say what code enforces, what needs evidence, what may be inferred, and how to handle uncertainty. If retrying, set a cap and stop rule.
guardrails.example: Leave unstated payment terms blank. Stop after two retests or when there’s no new fix to test.

docs.label: Documentation and debugging
docs.help: Link the exact applicable design sections and any guide, skill or repo file needed for this task. Use section anchors or line links at the relevant revision. If no design section applies, give the reason in Comments.
docs.example: Link directly to the approved invoice flag rule, including the paid and due-today cases.

model.label: Model
model.help: For an AI task, specify the model before dispatch. For deterministic runs, name the runner in Solution approach.

reasoning.label: Reasoning
reasoning.help: Required when an AI task needs a specific reasoning setting. Use the tool's supported label.

agent.label: Agent
agent.help: Before dispatch, confirm the executor. For a roster-based story, use the agent's stable roster ID. Leave blank during planning if unassigned.

stepId.label: Step ID
stepId.help: Give each new task a stable C- ID, such as C-01. Keep existing task IDs.

statusGuide.In design: The approach or scope still needs a decision.
statusGuide.Open: Designed and waiting to start. Check prerequisites before starting.
statusGuide.In progress: Work has started; the Task AC has not been verified.
statusGuide.Pass: The task met its Task AC and has evidence.
statusGuide.Blocked: A specific dependency or pending decision prevents progress. Record it in Comments.

modelGuidance: GPT-6.2 Astra or Claude Opus 5.5, as appropriate. Final code review follows review.md.
Claude Haiku prepares evidence. Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 handles difficult unresolved bugs.
TypeSafe Jev when explicit criteria and uncertainty handling are available.
displayContract: Proposed. Render columns and details in listed order; hide visible:false fields; never edit editable:false fields.
Read types, enums, required fields and limits from checklist.schema.json; show word counters from x-maxWords and the task total from x-taskWordLimit.
Run schema validation and x-applicationChecks on load and before save; block an invalid save and show the field or APP ID.
Omit blank optional fields instead of saving empty strings; show emptyText where defined.
Render requires and supports IDs as links. Show an Open task with an unclosed requires task as Waiting on its IDs without changing status.
Link supports to the criterion, check or scenario. Render task status, scenario results and story acceptance independently.
Show help and review text to people; show ai text on request.

scenarios.json.$comment: Field guidance for public definitions and private results. Validation and derivation rules are in scenarios.schema.json and results.schema.json. The displayFields section documents viewer-only labels. Do not author those keys in scenarios.json.

id.label: Criterion ID
id.help: Give each new criterion a stable A- ID, such as A-01. Keep existing criterion IDs.

version.label: Criterion version
version.help: Start at 1. Increase it when a change affects what this criterion’s verification proves.

actor.label: Actor
actor.help: Use an alias for the role or test account.

environment.label: Environment
environment.help: Use an alias for a required environment.

fixtures.label: Fixture aliases
fixtures.help: List aliases for test records or files. Resolve them in restricted storage.

actions.label: Actions
actions.help: List the execution and verification steps once. Name the surface when it changes a step.

surfaces.label: Required coverage
surfaces.help: Select every surface that must pass. Use a separate criterion if a surface needs a materially different setup or procedure.

startingState.label: Starting state
startingState.help: Include the preconditions and any setup needed to reproduce the case.

expectedResult.label: Expected result
expectedResult.help: State every required outcome, including records, rejection reasons, and exceptions.

assertions.label: Surface assertions
assertions.help: Shown for older scenario files. Put verification steps in Actions for new criteria.

supportingTasks.label: Supporting tasks
supportingTasks.help: Derived from checklist Supports links. Task status is separate from the scenario result.

surface.label: Surface
surface.help: Record the one required surface checked in this run.

revision.label: Tested revision
revision.help: Record the exact build, release or commit tested.

result.label: Run result
result.help: Record Pass, Fail or Blocked based on the observation.

evidence.label: Evidence
evidence.help: Link the observation, trace or readback in restricted storage.

runAt.label: Run time
runAt.help: Record the date, time and offset.

method.label: Method
method.help: Choose Manual or Automated. Start with Manual.

runner.label: Runner
runner.help: Name the tool or use an alias for the tester when useful.

builderAgent.label: Builder agent
builderAgent.help: Record the canonical agent ID of the builder for the tested revision. Required on new runs.

testerAgent.label: Tester agent
testerAgent.help: Record the canonical agent ID of the independent tester. Required on new runs and must differ from the builder ID.

testedAs.label: Tested as
testedAs.help: Use the alias for the account or role used.

identityVerified.label: Identity verified
identityVerified.help: Set to true only when the role was confirmed.

environment.label: Environment
environment.help: Use the alias of the tested environment.

comments.label: Comments
comments.help: Explain what blocked the run or cite the run being corrected.

criterionId.label: Criterion ID
criterionId.help: Use the ID of the acceptance criterion tested.

criterionVersion.label: Criterion version
criterionVersion.help: Record the criterion version used for this run.

statusGuide.Pass: Every required surface passed on the selected build and current scenario version.
statusGuide.Fail: A required surface failed on the selected build and current scenario version.
statusGuide.Blocked: A required check could not finish. See Comments.
statusGuide.NOT RUN: A required surface has no applicable run result.
statusGuide.Stale: The displayed result belongs to a different build or scenario version.

displayContract: Show each criterion with its verification details and each required surface with its latest applicable result.
Derive results from the private records using the rules in results.schema.json. Display older evidence with its original version and build.
Resolve aliases only in an authorized local view. Publish the sanitized scenario definitions separately.
Keep scenario results distinct from task status and human acceptance.

id.label: Blocker ID
id.help: Give each new blocker a unique stable B- ID, such as B-01.

status.label: Status
status.help: Use Open until the obstacle is resolved. Use Closed after verifying the fix.

goal.label: Goal
goal.help: State what the actor is trying to do in fewer than 30 words.

blocker.label: Blocker
blocker.help: Explain what prevents progress in fewer than 30 words.

currentFix.label: Current fix
currentFix.help: Describe the proposed or verified fix in fewer than 30 words. Cite evidence when closing.

affectedIds.label: Affected IDs
affectedIds.help: Reference the task or criterion IDs affected by the blocker.

documentationUrl.label: Documentation
documentationUrl.help: Link to the most useful supporting documentation when available.

leadId.label: Implementation Lead
leadId.help: Reference the stable ID of the agent coordinating this story.

sharedGuardrails.label: Shared guardrails
sharedGuardrails.help: Record rules that apply to the whole team once.

agents[].id.label: Agent ID
agents[].id.help: Give each new agent a stable AI- ID, such as AI-01. Reuse it in checklist assignments and private results.

agents[].name.label: Agent name
agents[].name.help: Give the agent a readable display name.

agents[].role.label: Role
agents[].role.help: Name the agent’s role for this story.
agents[].role.authoring: Choose a role based on the work the story needs. Confirm it during human review.

agents[].instructions.label: Operating instructions
agents[].instructions.help: State the standing instructions and handoff rules for this agent.

agents[].authority.label: Authority
agents[].authority.help: State what the agent can decide and when to escalate.

agents[].guardrails.label: Agent guardrails
agents[].guardrails.help: Record any additional limits specific to this agent.

agents[].skills.label: Skills
agents[].skills.help: List the exact skills needed for this role.

agents[].tools.label: Tools
agents[].tools.help: List the approved tool or connector names used by this role.

agents[].runtime.platform.label: Platform
agents[].runtime.platform.help: Name the required app or platform when applicable.

agents[].runtime.model.label: Model
agents[].runtime.model.help: Name the model when this role requires a specific one.

agents[].runtime.reasoning.label: Reasoning
agents[].runtime.reasoning.help: Name the required reasoning setting using the platform’s supported label.

agents[].runtime.environment.label: Environment
agents[].runtime.environment.help: Use an approved environment name or public alias.

agents[].references[].title.label: Reference title
agents[].references[].title.help: Name the document, skill, or reusable package.

agents[].references[].location.label: Reference location
agents[].references[].location.help: Use a verified public HTTPS URL or a path relative to the story.
